@graph.headline: Spring Fence Repair: 7 Warning Signs Michigan Winters Left Behind on Your Wood Fence
@graph.description: Michigan winters are tough on wood fences. Learn the 7 warning signs of winter damage and when to repair vs. replace your fence in Oakland County.

mainEntity.name: What are the first signs of winter damage on a wood fence?

acceptedAnswer.text: The earliest signs are small cracks in boards, slight leaning of posts, loose panels, and rusted hardware. These problems start small but worsen quickly with spring rain and summer heat.

mainEntity.name: When should I repair my fence in Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Spring is the best time — ideally April or early May. The ground is soft, contractors have more availability, and you catch problems before summer storms make them worse.

mainEntity.name: How much does fence repair cost in Oakland County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Minor repairs typically run $150-$500. Post replacement ranges from $200-$400 per post. Major section repairs may cost $500-$1,500. Full fence replacement runs $2,500-$8,000 depending on materials and length.

mainEntity.name: How long does a wood fence last in Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: A well-maintained wood fence in Michigan typically lasts 10-15 years. Premium cedar fences with consistent maintenance can last 20+ years.

mainEntity.name: Does a fence increase property value?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Studies show homeowners typically recoup 30-70% of their fence installation cost at resale. Privacy fencing is the most valued type among homebuyers.

mainEntity.name: What causes fence posts to lean after winter?

acceptedAnswer.text: Frost heave — the freezing and expansion of soil around fence posts — is the primary cause. Michigan's 60-100 annual freeze-thaw cycles push posts out of alignment.

mainEntity.name: Is it better to repair or replace a fence?

acceptedAnswer.text: If less than 30% of your fence is damaged and the posts are solid, repair is usually more cost-effective. If more than 30% is damaged or the fence is 15+ years old, replacement often makes more financial sense.
